propositions: Negative caplog assertions silently pass when zero records are captured, creating fail-open coverage gaps that are invisible in test output and indistinguishable from genuine verification.

Logger propagation set to False process-globally by configure_logging() and install_stderr_handler() level changes are never restored, poisoning downstream tests in the same process and causing assertions to reach zero records deterministically or non-deterministically depending on run order.
Five negative-assertion caplog statements across the suite can report success while verifying nothing, and this condition is undetectable from a green test run without instrumentation.

An autouse fixture guard that asserts logging.getLogger("rebar").propagate==True at test setup and restores both propagation and logger level at teardown converts silent fail-open into loud fail-closed detection at the source.

After instrumentation confirmed all five negative assertions were reached with propagate=True in a full run, the guard mechanism additionally contains the level vector by snapshotting and restoring logger levels, preventing future reintroduction of the class.
